chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Holder's $5 fine and the night off to hear Armstrong
summary: The band skips work to hear Armstrong; the ballroom owner gets a local band so Holder's men can go.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So, you know -- and he knew, he also knew Holder, the leader of our band, trumpet player. He said, "Old T. still got them good chops?" I said, "Yeah, he's a good player." I think it was around 1931 and that night, I have to tell you this, too, because we had a rehearsal later on that afternoon and Holder kind of felt like some of the guys wouldn't be coming to work that night. So he says, "Anybody that won't come to work --" we was playing out at this big beautiful ballroom "that won't come to work tonight, it's going to cost him $5.00," which was a lot of money then, you know, to compare it to -- I mean, to that day.

So I says, "Well, here's my five." I says, "I just met Pops," I said, "and I'm going to go hear him play tonight." I think we had about 13 pieces in the band. Earl Bostic was in the band. So he had about 13 five-dollar bills.
Everybody said they wouldn't go, wouldn't come to work. He got a little upset and he went and told the owner of the ballroom -- his name was Fogenberg -- so he

said, "Mr. Fogenberg," he says, "you know, I'm running into a little snag. Everybody want to -- the guys in the band want to hear Louie Armstrong tonight." So he says, "Oh, yeah?" He says, "Yeah." So he says, "I don't know what --" he says, "They've told me already. I fined them and they've already paid their fines." He says, "I don't know what to do." So he kind of hesitated for a while, I understand, then he finally told Holder, he says, "Well, I tell you what you do. If you find me a good dance band that can play some music here, a local band, tonight," he says, "I'll let all of you off and tomorrow night, you all come out to my place and listen to Louie Armstrong. I'll have Louie here on your gig," jokingly, you know.
